subject: Conditional Uplift & Stabilized Rate Addendum
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@dataharbor.com>, Brian Lee <brian.lee@dataharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional Uplift & Stabilized Rate Addendum

Hi Maria / Brian,

Thanks again for the productive renewal call last week. Attached is a short addendum proposal that aims to address DataHarbor's concerns about seasonal peak risk while keeping unit economics predictable for the year ahead. High level:

- Capacity buffer: a one-time committed uplift of 20% over your current average monthly consumption, available as burstable capacity through Q4 2027.
- Stabilized rate: we hold the current per-token/embedding rate for up to 12 months for consumption within the committed + buffer band.
- True-up and credits: if actual usage stays below committed volumes across the first 6 months, we apply a retro credit on next invoice; if usage exceeds the buffer consistently, overage rates apply with a tiered discount schedule.
- Conditional rollback: if you commit to a 12 month term and the uplift, Redwood provides a one-time onboarding credit of $25k applied over three invoices.

I attached the addendum (DataHarbor_Renewal_Addendum_v1.pdf) and a quick capacity estimate I asked Ben to validate. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync on Thursday to walk through the model and finalize commercial terms? Proposed times: 10:00 AM PT or 2:00 PM PT.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Conditional Uplift & Stabilized Rate Addendum

Thanks, Kimberly — appreciate the summary and the draft addendum. A few clarifying questions before we lock a time: 

1) Trigger definition: what constitutes "consistently exceeds the buffer"? Is that monthly, quarterly, or rolling 90 days?
2) Credits: are the retro credits automatic or do we need to submit usage reports to apply them? Our finance team wants an explicit flow.
3) Impact on invoices: will the uplift be billed pro-rated for the remainder of the current quarter?

We're generally aligned with the concept but need the mechanics so Procurement can approve. 2pm PT on Thursday works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite if you confirm.

Hi Maria / Brian,

Following up with the capacity and billing mechanics so Procurement/Finance have what they need ahead of Thursday's call. I validated the uplift model against your last 12 months of consumption:

- "Consistently exceeds the buffer" = any 3-month rolling window where average usage > committed + buffer. If that condition is met, overage pricing applies for the following month (with the first month as a grace period).
- Retro credits are automatic: Redwood will run an automated reconciliation at the 6-month mark and apply any credit to the next invoice; DataHarbor does not need to submit reports, though you can request the reconciliation export.
- Billing: the uplift is pro-rated from the effective date of the addendum for the remainder of the quarter. We'll show committed uplift, buffer, and any credits as separate line items on the invoice for transparency.

I attached a short capacity estimate workbook (capacity_estimate_2027.xlsx) with per-month scenarios (baseline, +20% uplift, +40% peak) and an example invoice that shows where the $25k onboarding credit would be applied.

David — tagging you to confirm the billing flow and that Redwood Finance can route the onboarding credit across three invoices as proposed.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Maria / Procurement team,

Great — thanks for the clarifying questions and Ben for the detail. Per our call earlier today we captured the following agreed points:

- Trigger definition: 3-month rolling average above committed + buffer will move usage into overage pricing after a one-month grace period.
- Credits: automatic 6-month reconciliation; export available on request.
- Billing: uplift pro-rated from effective date; committed uplift and credits shown as separate invoice line items.
- Onboarding credit: $25k applied across next three invoices.

I’ve uploaded the finalized addendum with these clarifications and a DocuSign envelope for signatures: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABC123456. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/2499/deal/54231 (please add the Procurement PO number when you sign).

1) Procurement to sign the DocuSign by EOD 2027-07-02.
2) Once signed, Redwood will pro-rate the uplift effective 2027-07-05 and apply the first installment of the onboarding credit on the next invoice.
3) Ben will deliver the reconciliation export at month 6 (automated) and share the report with Maria and your finance contact.

If Procurement needs any redlines related to invoicing language or PO flow, loop David (david.kim@redwood.com) and we’ll triage quickly.

Thanks — looking forward to another year with DataHarbor.
